title: Bint al-sahn (Yemeni layered honey cake)

ingredients.name: ghee, melted, plus extra for serving

steps: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar and salt, then add the eggs and warm milk and knead for 10 minutes to a soft, elastic dough. Rest, covered, for 1 hour.
Divide the dough into 8 portions and roll each into a very thin round, about the size of your baking pan.
Brush a deep round 24 cm pan with ghee and layer in the rounds one at a time, brushing each with ghee and stacking them.
Brush the top with an egg wash if you like, sprinkle with black seeds, and bake at 180 C for 30 to 35 minutes until deep golden brown.
Pour hot ghee over the top as soon as it comes out, then drizzle with warm honey.
Cut into wedges and serve warm with tea.

title: Fahsa (Yemeni shredded lamb stew)

ingredients.name: lamb shoulder or shanks, on the bone

steps: Simmer the lamb with half the onion, 2 cloves of garlic and the pepper in the water for 1.5 hours, skimming the surface, until the meat falls from the bone.
Lift out the meat and shred it, discarding the bones, and keep the broth.
Fry the rest of the onion in the ghee until golden, then add the remaining garlic, grated tomatoes, coriander, cumin and cardamom, and cook for 8 minutes until thick.
Add the shredded meat and 600 ml of the broth and simmer for 15 minutes, until the sauce is rich and reduced. Season with salt.
Serve bubbling hot in a heavy pot, topped with fresh coriander and zhug, with flatbread for scooping.

title: Fatoot samneh (Yemeni bread fried in ghee with eggs and honey)

ingredients.name: flatbreads (malawach, paratha or pita), torn into pieces

steps: Melt the ghee in a wide frying pan over medium heat.
Add the torn bread and fry, turning, for 3 to 4 minutes until it is golden and crisp at the edges.
Crack the eggs over the bread, add a pinch of salt, and stir gently until the eggs are just set.
Slide the mixture onto a plate and drizzle with the honey.
Scatter with the black seeds and serve hot with sweet tea.

title: Haneeth (Yemeni slow-roasted spiced lamb)
steps: Mash the garlic with the spices, salt and melted ghee to a thick paste and rub it thoroughly over the lamb. Leave it covered for 4 hours or overnight in the fridge.
Lay the onion and tomatoes in a deep roasting tin, set the lamb on top and pour in the water.
Seal the tin tightly with foil and roast at 160 C for 3.5 hours, until the meat pulls apart with a fork.
Meanwhile, cook the rice and, in the last 10 minutes, ladle in some of the roasting juices.
Uncover the lamb and roast for 15 minutes more at 220 C to brown the outside.
Serve the lamb on a bed of the rice, scattered with fresh coriander.

title: Hawaij (Yemeni spice blend for soups and stews)
steps: Toast the cumin, peppercorns, coriander, cardamom and cloves in a dry pan over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes, until fragrant.
Tip the spices onto a plate and let them cool completely.
Grind them in a spice grinder or mortar to a fine powder, then mix in the turmeric.
Store in an airtight jar away from light for up to 3 months.
Use 1 to 2 tsp in meat soups, stews and rice dishes, such as saltah, mandi and haneeth.

title: Hulbah (Yemeni whipped fenugreek dip)

ingredients.name: fenugreek seeds, soaked for 8 to 12 hours in plenty of water

steps: Drain the soaked fenugreek and rinse well, discarding the soaking water, which carries most of the bitterness.
Blend the seeds with the cold water, garlic, lemon juice and salt for a few minutes until you have a pale, frothy, almost mousse-like mixture.
Check the taste and adjust with more lemon juice or salt.
Spoon into a bowl and top with zhug and diced tomato.
Serve at once, as the froth settles quickly, with flatbread or on top of stews.

title: Lahoh (Yemeni spongy pancake bread)

ingredients.name: warm water, or a little more if needed
honey and butter, or a stew, to serve

steps: Whisk the flour, semolina, yeast, sugar and salt together, then whisk in the warm water until you have a smooth, thin batter.
Cover and leave in a warm place for 1 hour, until frothy and bubbly.
Heat a non-stick pan over medium heat and wipe it lightly with oil.

Pour in about 120 ml of batter and swirl to make a pancake about 18 cm wide. Cook on one side only, covered, for 2 to 3 minutes until the surface is covered in holes and set, with no wet batter remaining.
Slide the lahoh out, pale side up, and stack with the rest.
Serve with honey and butter, or use to scoop up stews, or tear and use in shafoot.

title: Malawah (Yemeni layered flatbread)

ingredients.name: honey, cheese or eggs, to serve

steps: Mix the flour, salt, sugar and yeast, add the water and 1 tbsp ghee, and knead for 8 minutes into a soft, smooth dough. Cover and let it rise for 1 hour.
Divide the dough into 6 balls and rest them for 10 minutes.
Roll or stretch one ball into a very thin round sheet and brush it with ghee. Fold it into a square, brushing ghee between each fold, to create layers.
Gently roll the folded square out a little to around 20 cm and repeat with the rest.
Cook the breads on a hot, lightly greased griddle for 2 to 3 minutes per side until golden brown and flaky.
Serve warm with honey, cheese, eggs or stew.

title: Mandi (Yemeni slow-cooked lamb with spiced rice)

ingredients.name: lamb shoulder or leg, on the bone, in large pieces

steps: Mix the spices, garlic and salt with 2 tbsp of the ghee to make a paste, and rub it all over the lamb. Marinate for at least 2 hours.
Place the lamb on a rack set in a roasting tin with a few spoons of water, cover tightly with foil, and roast at 160 C for 2.5 to 3 hours until the meat is very tender.
Fry the onion in the remaining ghee until golden, then add the soaked, drained rice and stir for 2 minutes.
Pour in the water, including the juices from the roasting tin, with a little salt, and cook, covered, on low heat for 18 minutes, then rest off the heat for 10 minutes.
Stir in the raisins and pile the rice onto a large platter, then lay the lamb over the top.
Serve with tomato sauce or zhug and a simple salad.

title: Masoob (Yemeni banana and bread pudding)

ingredients.name: soft flatbreads, torn into small pieces

steps: Place the torn bread in a large bowl and pour the melted ghee over it, tossing well.
Mash the bananas with a fork until they are a thick puree and fold them into the bread, mashing it all together into a soft, thick pudding.
Spread the mixture onto a large plate or shallow bowl.
Drizzle generously with honey and spoon on the cream.
Top with the dates and a pinch of cardamom, scatter with black seeds, and serve right away.

title: Naqe'e al zabib (Yemeni chilled raisin drink)
steps: Rinse the raisins and place them in a jug with the water and cardamom.
Cover and refrigerate for 8 to 12 hours, until the water turns a deep golden-brown colour and tastes sweet.
Press and lightly crush the raisins against the jug to release more flavour, then strain.
Serve over ice, sweetening only if needed. Drink within a day and keep it in the fridge, as soaked raisins ferment quickly.

title: Qishr (Yemeni spiced coffee-husk tea)
steps: Bring the water to a boil in a pot with the ginger, cinnamon and cardamom, and simmer for 5 minutes.
Add the coffee husks and simmer gently for 5 more minutes, then remove from the heat.
Cover and steep for 10 minutes so the flavours develop.
Strain into cups and sweeten to taste.
Serve hot, as is traditional after a meal.

title: Saltah (Yemeni lamb stew with fenugreek froth)

ingredients.name: lamb shoulder, cut into pieces on the bone
hawaij spice blend (or 1 tsp each cumin, black pepper and turmeric)

steps: Brown the lamb in a little oil in a heavy pot, then add the onion and half the garlic and cook until soft.
Stir in the tomato paste, tomatoes, hawaij and salt, then pour in the water. Simmer, covered, for 1.5 hours until the lamb is very tender.
Add the potatoes and green pepper and simmer for another 20 minutes.
Meanwhile, drain and rinse the soaked fenugreek, then whisk or blend it with 150 ml of cold water, the rest of the garlic and the lemon juice until it becomes a light froth (hulbah).
Transfer the hot stew to a heavy bowl, spoon the fenugreek froth over the top, and add a spoon of zhug.
Serve at once, scooping it up with flatbread and eating it with rice.

title: Shafoot (Yemeni lahoh with spiced yogurt)

ingredients.name: lahoh or soft flatbreads, torn into pieces
plain yogurt (or 300 g yogurt plus 200 ml buttermilk)
a few drops of oil, to finish

steps: Stir the yogurt with the garlic and salt until smooth, thinning it with a splash of water or buttermilk to a pourable consistency.
Fold in the spring onions, mint and coriander.
Lay the torn lahoh in a shallow dish or large bowl.
Pour the yogurt mixture over the bread and let it soak for 10 minutes so the bread softens.
Spoon zhug over the top, scatter with the diced tomato, and finish with a few drops of oil.
Serve cold or at room temperature as a starter or light meal.

title: Shahi haleeb (Yemeni milk tea with cardamom)
steps: Bring the water to a boil with the cardamom, add the tea, and simmer for 3 minutes until strong and dark.
Add the milk and condensed milk and heat, stirring, until just below a boil.
Simmer very gently for 3 minutes, taking care it doesn't boil over.
Strain into cups and serve hot, adjusting the sweetness with a little more condensed milk if you like.

title: Zhug (Yemeni fresh green chilli and herb sauce)
steps: Put the chillies, coriander, parsley and garlic in a food processor and pulse until finely chopped.
Add the cumin, cardamom and salt and pulse again.
With the machine running, drizzle in the olive oil and lemon juice until you have a loose, vibrant green paste.
Taste, adjusting the salt and heat to your liking.
Store in a jar in the refrigerator, covered with a thin layer of oil, for up to a week. Serve with bread, stews and grilled meat.

title: Zorbian (Yemeni spiced chicken, potato and rice)
steps: Fry the onions in the oil in a wide pot until golden brown, then add the chicken and brown it on all sides.
Stir in the garlic, tomato paste and all the spices and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the potatoes, salt and about 300 ml of the water, cover, and simmer for 20 minutes until the chicken is nearly cooked.
Pour in the remaining water and bring to a boil, then add the rice, spreading it evenly under the liquid.
Cover and cook on very low heat for 20 minutes, until the rice is tender and has absorbed the liquid.
Let it rest for 10 minutes, then serve straight from the pot with a fresh tomato and cucumber salad.
